descriptionFromApi:
We are hiring a Senior Designer to own the design of what we publish: brand identity, campaigns, websites, pitch documents and presentations, product interfaces, and video.


This is a hands-on ownership role, not a support-only one. You own each idea through to the finish line: the concept, the direction, the design, and the oversight of delivery.


You take business and marketing briefs and turn them into creative concepts, then design them: brand identity, campaigns, websites, presentations and pitch documents, product interfaces and video.


You will lead a team of Graphic Designers, Video Editors and Software Engineers to work alongside you on execution. The role exists for the idea as much as the artwork, so what you conceptualise matters as much as what you produce.


Your core advantage is that you decide what the work should be, not only how to make it. You take a business problem and an audience and come back with an answer and a reason for it, built from reference you have gone and found rather than from what has been done before. That judgement is central to the role.


This is a fully remote role. We are open to candidates based anywhere.


WORKING HOURS (fully remote)

Monday to Friday: 9am to 6pm UK time (BST)

Saturday: 9am to 1:00pm UK time (BST)


THE ROLE


You will:

- Originate the concept. You are given a business problem and an audience, and you decide what the answer is, including when the answer is not the one that was asked for.

- Produce more than one real answer to a brief. Genuinely different directions, not three versions of the same idea, and an argument for which one is right for that audience.

- Build the creative direction for each brand and be able to say where it came from and what it is arguing, so that the work is a position rather than a preference.

- Bring reference and range. You look widely, well outside this sector and often outside design, and you can name precisely what you are taking from where.

- Make or reference the first version of everything: brand work, campaigns, websites, pitch documents, presentations, product interfaces, video and social.

- Design documents and presentations for leadership and institutional partners, where the design has to carry the credibility of the argument.

- Design and specify product and dashboard interfaces precisely enough for our engineers to build them: the screens, the states, the components, the behaviour.

- Art-direct video and photography: what gets shot, how it is cut, how the titles and captions look, how a piece is framed for each platform.

- Keep each brand internally consistent and distinct from the others, so that none of them read as a template.

- Review work produced alongside you by other designers, and give clear, specific feedback on it.

- Build the systems that make volume possible: type scales, colour, components, presentation masters and templates, so recurring work becomes fast and stays on standard.

- Work at pace across several brands publishing at once, and deliver to a schedule rather than to inspiration.

- Take an ambiguous brief, resolve what is unclear yourself, and come back with a finished answer rather than a list of questions.


The work spans several brands across international consulting, from research and advisory through to student-facing community work, and extends to whatever else across the business needs designing well. You are the person who makes sure the idea is right, the craft holds up, and the finished piece is excellent.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- 3+ years in a design role where you owned the work you produced, not just executed someone else's layouts.

- A spectacular portfolio with a visible point of view: work that could only have come from you.

- Ideas that are yours. At least one piece where you set the concept, and where you can say what you rejected on the way to it.

- Conceptual range. Given one brief you can produce genuinely different answers rather than variations on a single idea, and argue for the right one.

- Breadth of reference. You can say where your influences come from, and the strongest answers usually come from outside design.

- Real craft underneath the ideas: typography, layout, hierarchy, restraint. We will look at the work before we read the CV.

- Range across formats. Range matters more to us than depth in any single one.

- Comfort with the serious end of the register as well as the loud end. Both a considered document for a senior audience and a piece that stops a scroll.

- Strong presentation and document design. A substantial part of the output is decks and pitch documents.

- Working knowledge of interface design, enough to design a real screen and hand it to an engineer.

- The ability to art-direct video even if you do not edit it yourself, and an advantage if you do.

- Sustained output. The role carries a high volume of work across several brands at once.

- Excellent written and spoken English. You will be working directly with the founder and with senior external stakeholders.

- Comfortable working fully remote, to UK hours, with high autonomy.


NICE TO HAVE

- Motion design or video editing you do yourself: After Effects, Premiere, DaVinci, CapCut.

- Experience building or maintaining a design system.

- Front-end ability, even light: enough HTML and CSS to shape a page rather than hand it over and hope.

- Illustration, 3D or generative imagery as a personal strength.

- Experience designing for a data or analytics product.

- Experience running or briefing other designers, freelancers or an agency.

- Exposure to the education, study-abroad, student or youth sector.

- Personal work you make because you want to as a passion

Experience: 2 to 8 years

Location: HSR Layout, BLR

Most Strategy and Operations roles quietly turn into reporting jobs. You pull the numbers, format the decks, and remind people about deadlines. This is not that role.

This is the role for someone who wants to learn, at close range, how a fast growing company actually plans, prioritizes, and executes. You will work directly with the CEO and the leadership team on the problems that cut across functions, the ones no single team can solve alone. Your job is to turn ambiguity into a plan, and a plan into results.

For the right person, this also happens to be one of the best leadership educations available anywhere. People who do this job well at Hevo build the instincts of a real operator, and many go on to run things. But the simplest reason to take it is this: you get to work on what matters most, alongside the people who decide it.

What you will own:

1. The operational rhythm of the whole company. You will work with the CEO to keep the entire machine moving across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Engineering, HR, Solutions, and Support. You will run the OKR process with the leadership team, drive quarterly planning and goal setting, and track delivery so nothing important slips. You will be the person who can tell, on any given day, how healthy the organization really is and where attention is needed next.

2. The strategic projects that move the needle. You will partner with the CEO and other leaders to spot the initiatives that genuinely change the trajectory of the business, then own them end to end until they are big enough to stand on their own and get handed to a dedicated team. These are the bets that matter most, and you will be trusted to carry them.

3. Cross functional execution and alignment. You will be the connective tissue across functions, driving communication so the company moves as one. You will be a real thought partner to leadership on vision, priorities, and the hard tradeoffs. You will manage relationships with stakeholders inside and outside the company, and when needed, represent leadership in reviews.

Why this role is special:

Three things make this seat genuinely rare.

You get the full view. Most people spend a decade seeing one function. You will see all of them at once, from the vantage point of the executive team, inside a company growing fast enough to teach you something new every week.

You work on first of a kind problems. Nearly every problem you solve will be one you have not solved before. There is no playbook handed to you. You build the playbook. For the right person, that is the most fun part of the job.

You build an operators judgment. Custodian of rhythm, owner of strategic projects, thought partner to leadership. That is the exact muscle set strong operators and founders are made of. You will leave this role with judgment most people take many more years to develop.

What you will need to bring:

We hire for abilities first, because knowledge and skills can be taught and abilities are far harder to build. Here is what we are really looking for.

1. Stakeholder management. You build trust with people at every level and quickly read what actually drives them. People want to work with you, and they tell you the truth.

2. People leadership. You understand what good leadership looks like up close. You know how to find the right levers and use them to bring out strong performance, and you have nudged teams into action in a way that energized them.

3. First principles problem solving. You are sharp with data, analytics, and reasoning. You break unfamiliar problems down to their fundamentals and build your way back up to a clear answer.

4. Ownership. You take a problem and you get it solved, full stop. You enjoy the wins, you own the misses, and you fix them. High accountability, no excuses.

5. Outwork and outsmart. You bring operational rigour and intensity. You find the smarter path, and you also do the work.

6. Independent thinking. You form your own point of view from the inputs in front of you, build conviction, and have the courage to make the call.

7. High agency. You move things forward mostly through influence, rarely through authority. You align people around the company wide goal by convincing them, not commanding them.

Who tends to thrive here:
The people who do exceptionally well in this seat usually share a pattern. They are intensely curious about how businesses work. They are comfortable being thrown into something they have never done and figuring it out. They care more about the outcome than the credit. And they have the energy to keep going when a problem turns out to be harder than it first looked, because that is usually where the most interesting work begins.

  • We are seeking a Principal/Staff-level FPGA Engineer a recognized technical authority to own FPGA architecture for our state-of-the-art Communications Test Measurement products.
  • The successful candidate will define and drive end-to-end FPGA architecture, including make/buy tradeoffs on IP, floorplanning and timing closure strategy for multi-gigabit designs, and DFX approach, using Verilog/SystemVerilog/VHDL and industry-leading simulation, synthesis, place-and-route, and formal/UVM verification tools.
  • This person will serve as the final technical escalation point for FPGA design and debug issues across the team, mentor other FPGA engineers, and lead root-cause debug of silicon and board bring-up issues that could not be resolved elsewhere.

  • BS or MS degree in Electrical and/or Computer Engineering with a minimum of 12-15 years of relevant experience, including at least 5+ years specifically architecting and closing timing on multi-Gbps SerDes/transceiver-based FPGA designs.
  • Demonstrated expertise architecting and implementing high-speed FPGA designs using Verilog/SystemVerilog and/or VHDL required.
  • Deep, hands-on expertise with FPGA transceivers, hard IP, and PLLs including timing closure, equalization, and link debug at multi-Gbps rates required (not incidental exposure).
  • Demonstrated experience closing timing and debugging link-layer issues on high-speed Ethernet (10M to 1.6T) and IP protocol stacks in production designs.
  • Proven expertise with optical interfaces and modules (SFPs, QSFPs) in shipped products.
  • Deep working knowledge of VLANs, MPLS, VPLS, and Voice/Video over IP (VoIP, IPTV).
  • Extensive experience with AMD or Altera FPGA devices and their full implementation toolchains, including advanced timing closure and floorplanning techniques.
  • Proven experience with formal verification and/or UVM-based verification methodologies, not limited to directed testbenches.
  • Demonstrated track record of taking FPGA designs from architecture through volume production, including systems-level tradeoffs across the HW/FW boundary.
